description: You are an allergist-immunologist preparing a chest CT series for a clinical presentation on airway remodeling in severe asthma. The DICOM directory at /home/ga/DICOM/studies/airway_series/ should contain only chest CT images from a single CT study. However, during a recent PACS migration, several DICOM files from a completely different imaging modality (MRI brain scans) were accidentally mixed into this directory. These contaminating files belong to a different patient and modality entirely. You must identify which files do NOT belong in this CT series — they will have a different Modality tag, different patient information, or fundamentally different image characteristics — remove them from the directory (delete or move them to /home/ga/DICOM/quarantine/), and verify that only legitimate CT files remain. After cleaning the series, write a contamination report to /home/ga/DICOM/exports/contamination_report.txt documenting: how many contaminating files were found, what modality/patient they belonged to, and confirmation that the remaining files are all consistent CT images from the same study.

metadata.clinical_scenario: Series contamination cleanup for clinical presentation

injected_contaminants.source: MR brain scan files mixed into CT chest directory
injected_contaminants.distinguishing_features: Different Modality tag (MR vs CT), different PatientName/ID, different StudyDescription
